arcane

ar-KAYN · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Arcane is understood by only a select few; mysterious.

The tax form referenced an arcane subsection that even the accountant had to look up.

Example

Only a handful of longtime members still understood the club's arcane bylaws about who could nominate a new officer.

Arcane fits knowledge or rules kept within a small, specialized group -- not necessarily complicated, just rarely shared outside it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

recondite: Recondite points at depth: subject matter so scholarly and difficult that few ever master it, however openly it is published. Arcane points at rarity instead -- arcane knowledge survives with only a select few, and it may be quite simple once someone finally shares it. Recondite is hard; arcane is scarce.

mystifying: Mystifying describes an effect on you right now: something baffles you and you cannot make sense of it. Arcane describes the knowledge itself -- held by only a select few, whether or not it puzzles anyone today. A card trick is mystifying to a whole audience; an arcane bylaw is perfectly clear to the one clerk who still knows it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

common: known to or shared by everyone

mainstream: regarded as normal, ordinary, and widely accepted

Where it sits · how hidden the knowledge is

specialized → arcane → occult

specialized vs. arcane: Specialized sits below arcane: specialized knowledge belongs to one field but is openly taught to anyone who joins it, while arcane knowledge has thinned out until only a select few still hold it.

occult vs. arcane: Occult goes beyond arcane -- arcane knowledge is merely rare, still understood by a scattered few, but occult knowledge is intentionally hidden from all but a select initiated few.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — arcan: hidden, secret (Latin arcanus, from arca 'chest')

suffix — -e: adjective ending carried over from Latin

Put it together: Arcane comes from Latin arcanus, "secret," itself related to arca, "a locked chest" -- something arcane is knowledge kept locked away from most people.

Use the root in a new word: ark: In the old story, animals boarded the ark two by two before the flood waters rose.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Arcane suggests knowledge that's rare or old-fashioned enough that almost no one still understands it, more than knowledge that's simply hard.
